focus: Security and network exposure: Tailscale Serve vs Funnel vs WebSocket bridge, relay authN/authZ, containment, audit
noveltyJustification: 5 of 6 findings fully new; finding 3 extends iteration-2/3 approval and ledger rules to the security plane.
keyQuestions: Which security and network exposure model is safe for a coding agent with workspace tool authority?
answeredQuestions: Which security and network exposure model is safe for a coding agent with workspace tool authority?
ruledOut: Tailscale Funnel as the exposure path
direct public WebSocket bridge as the default

label: Serve is the correct exposure: tailnet-only, identity-aware, auto-TLS, PROXY protocol; Funnel is public-internet and rejected for an agent relay.
Tailnet identity is reachability, not authorization; OWASP WebSocket checklist applies fully (wss-only, handshake auth, exact Origin allowlist, per-message authZ, rotation, rate limits).
Relay needs per-action authorization matrix gating privileged RPC actions (direct bash, cross-workspace switch) with audit and payload-digest-bound approvals.
Workspace containment: OS sandbox/least-privilege child, session files sensitive, metadata-only retention with digests for dedup.
Public WebSocket bridge viable only with full OWASP layer; strictly more attack surface than Serve.
Audit and incident response are design elements: security event logging without tokens/payloads, rotation/revocation, OWASP test list.

direction: Tailscale Funnel as the exposure path
reason: Public-internet listeners without per-visitor identity; violates least privilege for an agent relay.
It authenticates reachability only; per-action authZ still required.

direction: direct public WebSocket bridge as the default
reason: Strictly more attack surface than Serve; only with full OWASP layer for non-tailnet users.
Metadata-only retention with digests for dedup is the safer default.

label: Approval extension is a trust control: admin-owned, hash/version-pinned, fail-closed for side-effect tools; UI alone is not a security boundary.
